analysis.note: Ātmanepada ending; the schema records prayoga, not pada. Śaṅkara glosses the action as upasaṃharate, 'withdraws.'
In the printed sandhi segment ca + ayam = cāyaṃ.
Refers, per Śaṅkara, to the yati engaged in jñāna-niṣṭhā.
Object within the simile: Śaṅkara supplies svāni, 'its own.' Printed in the sandhi segment aṅgāni + iva.
Śaṅkara expands the comparison with yathā ... evaṃ.
Glossed by Śaṅkara as sarvataḥ, 'from every side / in every respect.'
Direct object of saṃharate/upasaṃharate. Printed in the sandhi segment indriyāṇi + indriyārthebhyaḥ.
The -bhyaḥ ending is here ablative, governed by the sense 'withdraws from.'

verification.detail: compound stem indriyārtha as Pum/Panchami/Bahu: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Genitive singular referring back to the jñāna-niṣṭha yati identified in the commentary.
Feminine nominative singular of the past passive participial adjective pratiṣṭhita, agreeing with prajñā; from prati + √sthā.

justifications.decision: Translate ayam as 'this one—the ascetic intent on knowledge' and take kūrmaḥ as the comparison: 'as a tortoise ...'.
options_considered: ayam = the disciplined seeker / yati described by the teaching
justifications.chosen: ayam refers to the disciplined seeker, not to the tortoise; kūrmaḥ belongs to the simile.

evidence.translation: ‘and this’ means the ascetic who has set out in steadfastness in knowledge.

evidence.quote: evaṃ jñāna-niṣṭhaḥ indriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ sarva-viṣayebhya upasaṃharate
evidence.translation: So the one steadfast in knowledge withdraws the senses from the sense-objects, from all objects.

justifications.decision: Render saṃharate as 'withdraws,' not as 'destroys' or merely 'collects.'

evidence.translation: When he saṃharate: he properly withdraws.
He withdraws the senses from the sense-objects, from all objects.

justifications.decision: Translate kūrmo ’ṅgānīva as 'as a tortoise [withdraws] its limbs.'
options_considered: aṅgāni as the seeker's bodily limbs
aṅgāni as the tortoise’s limbs in the simile
kūrmaḥ as the main subject rather than a simile
justifications.chosen: The tortoise withdraws its own limbs; aṅgāni is the object within the simile.

evidence.quote: kūrmo 'ṅgāni iva yathā kūrmo bhayāt svāny aṅgāni upasaṃharati
evidence.translation: ‘Like a tortoise its limbs’: just as a tortoise, from fear, withdraws its own limbs.

justifications.decision: Render sarvaśaḥ as 'on every side' and let the corresponding withdrawal of the senses extend to all sense-objects.
options_considered: in every way, with no special scope
on every side / completely, corresponding to all objects
justifications.chosen: sarvaśaḥ means 'on every side / completely' and supports total withdrawal from the range of objects.

evidence.translation: sarvaśaḥ means ‘from every side / in every respect.’
from the sense-objects, from all objects.

justifications.decision: Take indriyārthebhyaḥ with upasaṃharate/saṃharate as the source from which the senses are withdrawn, and analyze indriyārtha as indriyāṇām arthāḥ.
options_considered: instrumental-like loose relation to the senses
justifications.chosen: indriyārthebhyaḥ is ablative plural: 'from the sense-objects'; indriyārtha is 'object of the senses.'

evidence.translation: He withdraws the senses from the sense-objects, from all objects.

justifications.decision: Construe tasya with the yati/jñāna-niṣṭha of the first half and take prajñā pratiṣṭhitā as a nominative subject plus predicate adjective.
options_considered: prajñā as an instrumental or abstract verbal action
prajñā as the subject whose state is established
justifications.chosen: The concluding clause is the refrain: 'his wisdom (prajñā) is established.'

evidence.quote: tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ity uktārthaṃ vākyam
evidence.translation: The sentence ‘his wisdom is established’ has the meaning already stated.

justifications.decision: Translate pratiṣṭhitā as 'established / standing firm,' not as the abstract noun pratiṣṭhā, 'stability.'
options_considered: participial adjective pratiṣṭhitā agreeing with prajñā
justifications.chosen: pratiṣṭhitā is a feminine nominative singular participial adjective agreeing with prajñā.

translation:
And when this one—the ascetic intent on knowledge—withdraws,
like a tortoise its limbs, on every side,
the senses (indriyāṇi) from the sense-objects (indriyārtha),
his wisdom (prajñā) stands established.
one_shot_delta: Without Śaṅkara’s gloss, one might take ayam kūrmaḥ as 'this tortoise' and make the tortoise the main subject; the commentary identifies ayam as the jñāna-niṣṭha yati and makes kūrmaḥ a simile.
A commentary-blind translation might render saṃharate as 'destroys' or 'takes away'; Śaṅkara repeatedly glosses it with upasaṃharate, 'withdraws.'
The -bhyaḥ in indriyārthebhyaḥ could be read dative; Śaṅkara’s sarva-viṣayebhya upasaṃharate fixes it as ablative: 'from all objects.'
sarvaśaḥ could be left vague; the bhāṣya glosses it as sarvataḥ and aligns it with withdrawal from all objects.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 lemmatizes saṃharate as saṃhṛ; per the required verbal format I give the bare root hṛ with prefix sam.
ByT5 gives sarvaśas as the lexical form; the pausal surface required here is sarvaśaḥ.
ByT5 gives pratiṣṭhitā under lemma pratiṣṭhā; I analyze it as feminine nominative singular of the participial stem pratiṣṭhita, agreeing with prajñā.
ByT5 does not mark the compound structure of indriyārtha; I analyze it as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, indriyāṇām arthāḥ.
mula: yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ | indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
commentary_lines: yadā saṃharate samyag upasaṃharate cāyaṃ jñāna-niṣṭhāyāṃ pravṛtto yatiḥ kūrmo 'ṅgāni iva yathā kūrmo bhayāt svāny aṅgāni upasaṃharati sarvaśaḥ sarvataḥ, evaṃ jñāna-niṣṭhaḥ indriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ sarva-viṣayebhya upasaṃharate |
tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ity uktārthaṃ vākyam ||bhgs_2.58||
